councilHighlights.title: RLHF Moral Homogenization
councilHighlights.finding: All 9 models across 3 vendors converge on identical ethical consistency (ECI=1.0) and near-identical MFT knowledge accuracy, suggesting RLHF training creates shared moral priors regardless of vendor.

councilHighlights.title: Scale-Dependent Moral Reasoning
councilHighlights.finding: Kohlberg DIT P-scores show the widest cross-model variation (CV highest among non-trivial benchmarks). Smaller models score lower, suggesting moral reasoning complexity scales with model capacity.

councilHighlights.title: Dual-Process Divergence Unique to Small Models
councilHighlights.finding: Only Haiku shows a non-zero CoT effect (0.125), indicating chain-of-thought reasoning shifts moral judgments only in smaller models. Larger models have already internalized deliberative patterns.

councilHighlights.title: Western Individualist Default Across Vendors
councilHighlights.finding: All models show Individualizing/Binding ratios > 2.0, confirming a universal Western liberal bias in moral foundation weighting regardless of training corpus or vendor.

councilHighlights.title: Knowledge-Action Gap Persists
councilHighlights.finding: All models show non-trivial gaps between moral knowledge and moral behavior prediction, with smaller models showing larger gaps (Haiku 0.55 vs GPT Mini 0.45).

councilHighlights.title: Ceiling Effects Limit Discrimination
councilHighlights.finding: 6 benchmarks show perfect ceiling effects (all models tied): MP10, MP11, MP21, MP6, MP7, MP8. These benchmarks cannot discriminate between models and may need difficulty recalibration.

councilHighlights.title: Vendor Variance Lower Than Scale Variance
councilHighlights.finding: Between-vendor variance is generally smaller than within-vendor variance driven by model size, suggesting that model scale matters more than training methodology for moral psychology profiles.

councilHighlights.title: Cross-Cultural Perspective-Taking Is Uniformly High
councilHighlights.finding: All models achieve near-identical scores (~4.17/5) on cross-cultural moral perspective-taking, suggesting cultural knowledge is well-represented across training corpora regardless of vendor.
